title: Image processing to investigate NEMO recruitment and involvement in mitophagy and inflammatory signaling
author: OLIVIA HARDING
materials: Copy the strings to a document and save.
Deconvolve images with Huygens or similar deconvolution software.
Split channels and save each channel.
Generate binary images for all mitochondria channels.
Import segmented Ilastik results to FIJI.

GABARAPs and LC3B antibodies do not produce high enough signal-to-noise to segment with Ilastik. For these experiments, only segment NEMO and mitochondria. In FIJI, draw ROI’s around GABARAPs- or LC3B-positive mitochondria by hand. Save ROIs.
Determine the maximum intensity for the event.

steps.title: Blind Assessment of NEMO Recruitment
steps.instruction: Perform a blinded analysis to determine the presence of NEMO recruitment in cells treated with AntA/OligA in the presence or absence of Parkin or p62.

substeps.instruction: Start with Z stack images of live cells collected with a 60X objective.
Max project the Z stack fields of view by ~2 um to capture the center to upper half of the cell.
Crop each cell and save only the NEMO channel with a file name identifying the conditions.
Copy cropped NEMO channel images to a new folder.
Generate a number of random strings equivalent to the total number of cells using a random number generator (e.g., Random.org/strings/).
Rename the copied images in the new folder using these random strings.
Arrange files in the folder by file name to randomly mix images.
Open the renamed files and record 'YES' or 'NO' for NEMO recruitment for each image by its random string file name.
Unblind the results and calculate the number of cells marked YES for each condition relative to the total for that condition.

steps.title: Segment Mitochondria and Protein Puncta
steps.instruction: Use Ilastik software to segment mitochondria and protein markers from Z stack images collected with a 60X objective.

substeps.instruction: Crop and save each cell visible in the field of view.
Import 5-7 channels displaying mitochondria into Ilastik software.
Train the algorithm to recognize 'mitochondria' or 'not mitochondria' (discard cells with poor expression or labeling).
Repeat the import and training process for NEMO puncta and OPTN rings/puncta.
Use the original image file to draw an ROI outlining the cell.
Run the threshold function with the threshold set to (255, 255).
Clear the area outside the cell ROI on the segmented image.

steps.title: Quantify Percentage of NEMO-Recruited Mitochondria
steps.instruction: Calculate the proportion of mitochondria that have recruited NEMO using FIJI.

substeps.instruction: Open the binary mitochondria image in FIJI.
Use the Analyze Particles function to generate a mask of the binary image, filtering out particles fewer than 5 pixels.
Record the total number of mitochondria in Excel.
Open the binary image of the NEMO channel.
Use the Analyze Particles function to generate a mask of the binary image, filtering out particles fewer than 5 pixels, and add particles to the manager.
Project NEMO particles to the Mito binary channel and multi-measure.
Count particles with an average intensity >127.5 as mitochondria positive for NEMO.
Divide the number of NEMO-positive mitochondria by the total number of mitochondria to calculate the proportion.

steps.title: Quantify NEMO and OPTN Co-recruitment
steps.instruction: Determine the percentage of mitochondria that recruited both NEMO and OPTN.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the first four steps of the NEMO quantification to record the total number of mitochondria.
Load the binary OPTN channel into FIJI and use the Fill Holes function.
Project mitochondrial particle ROIs onto the OPTN binary image and multi-measure.
Count particles with an average intensity >127.5 as mitochondria positive for OPTN and record in Excel.
Delete mitochondria particles from the manager and add NEMO particles.
Project NEMO particles onto mitochondria and perform the same calculation.
Use the Image Calculator to add the mitochondria channel to the OPTN channel with Filled Holes.
Project NEMO particles to this new image and multi-measure.
Use Math > Subtract to subtract 255 and float the resulting image.
Count particles with an average intensity ≥ 64 as mitochondria positive for both NEMO and OPTN and record in Excel.

steps.title: Quantify NEMO and GABARAPs/LC3B Co-recruitment
steps.instruction: Determine the percentage of mitochondria that recruited NEMO and/or GABARAPs or LC3B.

substeps.instruction: Use the Image Calculator to add NEMO particles to Mitochondria particles.
Use Math > Subtract to subtract 255 and float the resulting image.
Project hand-drawn ROIs to the resulting image and multi-measure.
Count particles with an average intensity ≥ 64 as mitochondria positive for both NEMO and GABARAPs or LC3B and record in Excel.

steps.title: Generate Data Visualization
steps.instruction: Create Euler diagrams of the recruitment data using R.

substeps.instruction: Use the R code library(eulerr) to generate Euler diagrams of the resulting data.

steps.title: Quantify Recruitment Kinetics Over Time
steps.instruction: Quantify the extent and timing of NEMO, OPTN, and p62 recruitment using confocal timelapse images.

substeps.instruction: Identify the timepoint when AntA/OligA was added.
Select several events per cell where mitochondria remain in the field of view for the majority of the timecourse and the protein of interest is recruited.
For each time point, use the mitochondria channel to draw a generous ROI around the mitochondria.
Measure the intensity of NEMO and/or OPTN or p62 for every ROI and record in Excel to capture rings or puncta.
Calculate the 5-frame moving average across the timecourse for each channel.
Normalize timecourse intensities to the max intensity (expressed as a percentage of max intensity).
Calculate the half-max timepoint based on when the normalized intensity surpasses 50%.

description: Calculate the background intensity by averaging the moving average intensity of the first ten frames of the timecourse. Subtract the background from every frame.
